xpam

xpam builds presence-absence matrices (PAMs) from species range polygons or occurrence records. A PAM is a sites-by-species binary table: rows are sites (raster cells or environmental bins), columns are species, and each entry is 1 (present) or 0 (absent). PAMs are a foundational data structure in macroecology and biogeography for computing species richness, range-diversity plots, co-occurrence analysis, and conservation prioritisation.

The package offers two scales of operation:

  • a dense small-input path (get_geo_pam()) that rasterises a terra::SpatVector onto a grid and returns a tibble;
  • a streaming native engine (C++17, OpenMP, GDAL optional) that never materialises a dense matrix — pam_incidence() returns the sparse PAM, pam_env_engine() returns marginals, and pam_jaccard() computes species- or site-wise Jaccard similarity directly from the same incidence. Proven at 22.5e9 occurrence pairs.

Installation 

# From CRAN
install.packages("xpam")

# Development version from GitHub
# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("alrobles/xpam")

GDAL is optional. When present at build time (has_gdal() reports it) the native raster engine links and streams vector sources directly; without GDAL the package still installs and the terra-based path works.

Quick Start 

library(xpam)

# Load example data: Rodentia of Mexico (downloaded on demand)
shp <- get_rodentia_mexico()

# Build a PAM at 1-degree resolution
pam_result <- get_geo_pam(shp, res = 1)
head(pam_result)
#> # A tibble: 6 × 42
#>       x     y Chaetodipus arenarius ...
#>   <dbl> <dbl>                 <dbl>
#> 1 -118.  23.5                     0
#> ...

A fully local example that needs no download:

square <- function(x0, y0, size = 2) {
  m <- matrix(c(x0, y0, x0 + size, y0,
                x0 + size, y0 + size, x0, y0 + size),
              ncol = 2, byrow = TRUE)
  terra::vect(m, type = "polygons", crs = "EPSG:4326")
}
ranges <- rbind(square(0, 0), square(2, 2))
ranges$sciname <- c("species_a", "species_b")
get_geo_pam(ranges, res = 1)

Main Functions

Function Description
get_geo_pam() Dense PAM from a SpatVector at a given resolution
pam_incidence() Sparse PAM (Matrix::dgCMatrix or i/j triplets) from any occurrence source
pam_env_engine() Streaming environmental PAM marginals from raster files
pam_env() Dense small-input environmental PAM
pam_jaccard() Species- or site-wise Jaccard similarity (optional thresholded edge list)
has_gdal() Report whether the build has GDAL support
get_rodentia_mexico() Example data: rodent ranges for Mexico
get_world_pca() WorldClim bioclimatic PCA raster (2 layers)

Documentation

Full documentation, reference and the introductory article live at https://alrobles.github.io/xpam/. Vignettes are published there and are deliberately not shipped in the CRAN tarball.
